Summary of what we heard:
- Primary requirement: private connectivity from ClearWave VPCs into Redwood for PII-sensitive inference.
- Preferred hosting: you're leaning toward Private VPC (private endpoints) vs our Hosted API because of data residency/isolation and audit controls. Dedicated capacity is still on the table if you need predictable throughput but want isolation at the GPU layer.
- Key networking asks: PrivateLink vs VPC peering, topology for egress to downstream vendors, and whether ClearWave needs static egress IPs for vendor allowlists.

Open questions / asks for NetOps call:
1) Confirm whether ClearWave prefers AWS PrivateLink (VPC Endpoint Services) or full VPC peering. Any platform preference (AWS vs GCP) we should plan for?
2) Do you require static egress IPs for requests originating from our infra to your vendors? If yes, please provide desired ranges or whether a small set of Elastic IPs is acceptable.
3) Who owns the firewall/allowlist (ClearWave netops, vendor, or third party)? Please share the contact if not Priya.
4) Estimated tenant/isolation model: single-tenant VPC per environment, or multiple tenants behind a shared endpoint?

Attachments: initial diagram + short checklist to help NetOps evaluate (networking_diagram_v1.png, privatelink_vs_peering_checklist.xlsx).

Thanks — if you can reply with the NetOps contact and any preliminary IP ranges, we’ll get the working session on the calendar and circulate a short agenda.

Subject: RE: Post-call recap — PrivateLink vs peering (technical note)

Alex / Karthik — quick technical note from Solutions that will help the NetOps conversation.

Short version: AWS PrivateLink (VPC Endpoint Service) avoids peering but does not by itself provide static source IPs for outbound egress to third-party vendors. If ClearWave requires static egress IPs from Redwood's side (so vendors see a stable source IP), we have two common patterns:

Option A — PrivateLink + NAT egress: Redwood's PrivateLink service handles inbound traffic to our endpoint; for outbound calls originating from our service to third-party vendors, we can egress through a NAT Gateway with an Elastic IP (EIP). This gives you stable outbound IPs but requires us to manage NAT/EIP mapping and routing.

Option B — VPC peering with shared egress: Peering allows native routing but means cross-account route table management. Peering alone doesn't solve multi-tenant static egress unless we provision a dedicated egress subnet with EIPs for traffic bound to specific vendors.

A few additional clarifying asks for NetOps:
- Can ClearWave accept a small set of Redwood-owned Elastic IPs for vendor allowlisting? (recommended for fastest delivery)
- If you need per-tenant IP separation, we should confirm how many distinct IP sets you require.
- Any outbound ports blocked by vendor firewalls? (e.g., 443 only)

I attached a short checklist that maps service model -> egress implications to help the call (privatelink_vs_peering_checklist.xlsx).

Proposed NetOps slots: Wed 11/18 10:00 PT or Thu 11/19 14:00 PT.

If those work, Karthik can lock the invite and we'll include an infra engineer to walk through the diagram.
